newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CASE TO INVEST $100 MLN IN BRAZIL PLANT.
newsitem.headline: CASE TO INVEST $100 MLN IN BRAZIL PLANT.

text.p: Case Corp of the United States will invest $100 million in Brazil to manufacture tractors and harvesters, a spokeswoman for the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said.
Case vice president for Latin America Andrew Graves announced the investment during a meeting with the ministry's secretary of industrial policy, Antonio Sergio Mello, she said.
Graves said the investment would be carried out by the year 2000 at Sorocaba in Sao Paulo state, where Case already has a factory producing machinery for the construction industry.

The new agricultural machinery production line is expected to have an annual capacity of 1,500 harvesters and 5,000 tractors, with the first models running off the factory line in the first quarter of 1998.
"The accord proves Case's confidence in the Brazilian agricultural market, one of the most promising in the world," said Case Brasil's agricultural division director Mario Hirose in a statement.
Industrial policy secretary Sergio said the plant would employ 200 people and create another 500 indirect jobs.
Case signed up to the Brazilian government's Car Industry Regime as "newcomers", allowing it to import components at reduced tariffs and enjoy some fiscal benefits.
